sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Even before coalition negotiations begin, Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman is pursuing a different strategy from Eisenkot's planned 48-seat 'national emergency government': a 61-seat government with the Haredi parties, or another election. Jerusalem Mayor Moshe Lion is reported to be mediating talks between Liberman and Haredi politicians. Eisenkot warned indirectly that anyone trying to sabotage government formation for personal rather than substantive reasons would be judged accordingly. [CONFIRMED CONTEXT] The formal mandate ceremony is Sunday Nov 8 at 17:00 Israel time (18:00 ) at the President's Residence; Eisenkot then has 28 days (plus a possible 14-day extension) to form a government; the new Knesset is sworn in Tuesday Nov 10. Eisenkot holds 67 recommendations (48 Change Bloc + 19 from Ra'am/Joint List) vs 46 for Netanyahu; 7 recommended no one.
sections.what_verified: 2 tiered families (Ynet T3, NDTV T3) for the update as a whole; CNN as attribution-only relay.
sections.what_disputed: Eisenkot's 67 endorsements do not translate into a 67-seat coalition -- the 19 Arab-party recommendations are for the mandate, not necessarily for joining a government; Liberman's Haredi route would need the ultra-Orthodox parties to accept a government that includes them while Eisenkot's conditions (universal service, recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation) may be unacceptable to parts of his own bloc. Netanyahu remains prime minister until a new government is sworn in.
sections.why_matters: Eisenkot won the mandate -- and on day one his own camp is already splitting over how to use it.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261108-0100-02 (Eisenkot mandate) -- IN-WINDOW (Ynet published 2026-11-08T00:20:09Z = 04:20 ; NDTV 07:05 IST = 05:35 ) -- Liberman rejects Eisenkot's minority government, pursues a 61-seat coalition with the Haredi parties instead; mandate ceremony today 17:00 Israel time (18:00 )

totw_analysis: Our read: Eisenkot won the mandate -- and on day one his own camp is already splitting over how to use it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Emergency government now with Arab-party backing, or a 61-seat coalition with the Haredi parties -- which path actually ends Netanyahu's rule?
